patch.value: ADR: one release per UTC day is architectural, not a policy gate - decide whether a manually triggered same-day release is a supported operation

Live verification 2026-07-31: the scheduled Auto Release run at 05:50:49Z succeeded, v2026.7.31 is the latest GitHub release, npm dist-tag latest resolves 2026.7.31, and both npx @unbrained/pm-cli@latest and bunx @unbrained/pm-cli@2026.7.31 report 2026.7.31. One release per day is working end to end on both package runners. The Auto Release workflow's issues:closed trigger is correctly fenced by its job-level if to the specific bot-authored blocker issue, and the four issue-triggered runs today all report skipped.

The open question is what should happen on a deliberate second release in one day, because two independent mechanisms currently forbid it and only one of them is a policy.

The policy gate is maybeSkipForSameDayRelease in scripts/release/run-release-pipeline.mjs:263-279, which lists local tags matching v<todayKey>* and skips with reason release_already_cut_today. It is evaluated unconditionally at line 423, so workflow_dispatch is gated exactly as the schedule is, and --allow-same-day-release was deliberately removed at lines 384-387 with the message directing operators to retry the existing tag through the Release workflow.

The architectural constraint is resolveVersion at lines 103-112, which fails unless the target version equals the current UTC date key. A second release on the same day would need a second distinct version, and the date-based scheme has no room for one: 2026.7.31 is already published and npm will not accept a re-publish. So even removing the policy gate would not enable a second same-day release; it would produce a version collision.

The stated intent - never two automatic releases per day unless manually triggered - is therefore not satisfiable today, and the gap is in the version grammar rather than in the guard. Three options, and this decision should pick one rather than leaving the intent and the implementation disagreeing.

First, ratify the current behaviour: one release per UTC day, full stop, with a partial failure recovered by retrying the existing tag rather than cutting a new version. This is what the code does and what the removal message already assumes; it costs nothing and makes the guard's unconditional evaluation correct by design rather than by accident.

Second, add a same-day ordinal: 2026.7.31.1 for the second cut of the day. This satisfies the stated intent, and it changes the version grammar everywhere it is parsed or compared - scripts/sync-versions.mjs, the padded-versus-unpadded comparison that once silently skipped releases, the changelog release-tag matching, plugin and marketplace manifests, and any consumer pinning a caret range. The cost is broad and the benefit narrow.

Third, keep one version per day and allow a manual re-run to amend the same version before it is published, which covers the real operational need - a same-day fix after a bad cut - without a new version at all.

The recommendation is the first option, with the third as the documented recovery path, because the operational need is amendment rather than a second release. Whichever is chosen, the guard's behaviour under workflow_dispatch should be stated in docs/RELEASING.md, since an operator today sees a manual dispatch skip with no explanation of why manual and scheduled behave identically.

One option is accepted and recorded in this decision with its rationale, and the rejected options are retained with the reason so the question is not reopened from scratch; docs/RELEASING.md states what a manual workflow_dispatch does when a release already exists for the current UTC day, and names the supported recovery path for a partial failure; If the ratify option is accepted, the unconditional evaluation of the same-day guard is documented as intentional at the call site so it is not later read as a bug and made dispatch-conditional; If the ordinal option is accepted, every version-parsing and version-comparison site is enumerated before any change lands, including the padded-versus-unpadded comparison that previously skipped releases silently; The decision records the live verification captured here - one successful scheduled run, one release, npm latest and both npx and bunx resolving it - as the baseline the policy is being decided against
